entry, so that frame unlocked the composer and froze the answer

# Support agent chat

## Problem Statement

The engine has since changed underneath the client in three ways. `hal-engine-single-terminal-frame` (#148) makes `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message, after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to an unrelated malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame drops the typing indicator and unlocks the composer mid-answer. `hal-engine-subprotocol-marker` (#150) stops echoing the client's subprotocol offer and selects only the reserved marker `hal.v1`, so a bare-token offer fails the handshake in both `ws` and Chromium and no customer could connect. The engine's error path now commits the last entry before the `error` frame,…

## Why

`044` clears the client's `busy` flag on `stream_end`, on an `error` frame, or on socket close - a correct reading of the engine's protocol doc as it stood at the time. `139` inverts that contract engine-side after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to a malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of an otherwise healthy stream: a client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame reads that unrelated frame as "your answer is finished" while the answer is still arriving, dropping the typing indicator and unlocking the composer mid-stream. Under `139` there is now exactly one terminal signal - `stream_end`, sent exactly once per accepted message, error or not - and that issue explicitly supersedes `044`'s client-side rule and queues this issue as the correct…

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the engine half - a sibling issue owns `stream_end` as the single terminal frame and the protocol doc inversion, and another owns committing open entries on every terminal path; what the error frame says and when its notice clears - owned by the Danish failure-messages work, this issue only guarantees `state.error` is still set; redefining `ChatErrorInfo.interrupted`, queued as its own task since both this change and the entry-commit fix invalidate its current computation point; suppressing or restyling an advisory error that arrives mid-healthy-stream - today's behavior of rendering it anyway is kept, any change there is a product question for the failure-messages work; reconnect and resume - the close branch's `busy` clearing is unchanged from `044`. Keep the chat busy through an error frame until stream_end or close

HAL Engine 0.3.0 ends every user_message with exactly one stream_end,
errored or not, and can send an unrelated error (an INVALID_MESSAGE
for some other malformed frame) between two deltas of a healthy
answer. The error branch cleared busy and stopped every streaming
entry, so that frame unlocked the composer and froze the answer
mid-sentence. It now only records the error; stream_end and a close
stay the run's terminators and keep their isStreaming sweep as the
backstop.

The web reducer treated any `error` frame as the end of the run: it cleared `busy` and stopped every streaming entry. Issue #191 and PR #290 (merged 2026-09-29, commit e131e7b) changed that. The error branch now only records the error, so `state.error` is still set. The client clears `busy` only on `stream_end` or on socket close. The reason is that HAL Engine 0.3.0 sends exactly one `stream_end` per accepted message, whether or not it errored. It can also send an unrelated `error`, such as an INVALID_MESSAGE for another malformed frame, in the middle of a healthy stream.
